status_history.reason: First structured draft from CASE-003 production evidence. Deep-sea particle HUD system, single-cyan accent strategy, glass data panels, and flowing light-dot networks extracted from a real historical data-visualization project. Includes the documented exhausted motif list from that project. No current HyperFrames rendering verification has been performed.

title: Deep Current HUD
summary: A cold deep-sea data center visual system using deep indigo radial depth, a single electric cyan accent, multi-layer floating particles, glass HUD panels, and light-dot data flows. Designed for high-density system, network, pipeline, and scale visualization.
best_for: user acquisition and growth data stories
system architecture and network topology explanations
real-time data monitoring and metric reveals
avoid_for: restrained editorial with minimal glow and no data density

canvas.tone: cold deep-indigo radial depth suggesting an underwater data center
canvas.background_policy: A deep indigo radial gradient creates infinite depth. Multi-layer particles float at different parallax depths. The canvas is never flat or empty; ambient depth is always present but recedes behind active data planes.

palette.strategy: Single electric cyan accent over a deep indigo field. All information encoding uses cyan brightness hierarchy. No secondary accent colors compete; state indicators use subtle saturation shifts within the cyan family.

roles.semantic: infinite cold depth and spatial context
roles.value_policy: deep indigo radial gradient, darkest at edges, subtle brightening at focal center

roles.semantic: the single active information and emphasis channel
roles.value_policy: electric cyan with three brightness tiers: full-cyan for primary data, mid-cyan for secondary labels, dim-cyan for ambient HUD chrome

roles.semantic: information container floating above the abyss
roles.value_policy: semi-transparent dark glass with subtle cyan edge light, never fully opaque

roles.semantic: precise measurement, coordinates, and technical annotation
roles.value_policy: monospace cyan-tinted white at the smallest readable size

roles.purpose: carry the primary metric, system name, or key finding
roles.style_relation: largest weight, full cyan brightness, geometric sans-serif for authority

roles.purpose: label panels, describe flows, and annotate data points
roles.style_relation: mid-weight, mid-cyan brightness, clean sans-serif subordinate to display

roles.purpose: render coordinates, task codes, timestamps, and precision values
roles.style_relation: smallest weight, dim-cyan tint, monospaced for alignment and technical texture

typography.local_fallback_policy: Detect available geometric sans-serif and monospace fonts locally. Verify glyph coverage for numeric, Latin, and CJK character sets. Monospace must render with consistent character width.

materials: deep indigo radial gradient field with parallax depth layers
multi-layer floating particles at distinct Z-depths
semi-transparent dark glass HUD panels with cyan edge
flowing light-dot networks along data paths
monospace coordinate scales and technical annotations
spatial_hierarchy: deepest particle layer as ambient depth
mid-depth HUD glass panels as information containers
foreground light-dot flows as active data paths
frontmost cyan primary metric or system label as focal point
visual_system.whitespace_policy: The abyss provides infinite depth; glass panels float within it with generous spatial separation. Never crowd panels against each other or against the frame edge. HUD elements respect a safety margin for overlay compatibility.

focus_policy.rule: One primary metric or system node owns the shot at full cyan brightness. All other HUD elements, particles, and flows operate at mid or dim cyan and recede into the depth hierarchy.

purposes: present a structured data set, system status, or metric group
give technical information a readable spatial home
scene_grammar.composition: One primary glass HUD panel floats center-frame at mid-depth. The panel contains a primary metric in full cyan, supporting labels in mid-cyan, and mono-scale annotations along its edges. Particles drift behind it; a light-dot flow may connect it to a secondary panel.
required_semantics: a real data set or system state with meaningful structure
a clear primary metric or status to anchor the panel
forbidden_uses: inventing task codes or coordinates for visual texture
stacking multiple competing full-cyan panels in one shot

purposes: show how data, requests, or resources move through a system
visualize topology, routing, or pipeline stages
scene_grammar.composition: System nodes appear as small cyan points or glass dots distributed across the frame. Light-dot flows travel along connecting lines between nodes. The flow direction, speed, and density encode data volume or priority. One node or path is at full cyan brightness as the focal point.
required_semantics: a real directional or relational structure
meaningful differentiation between nodes or flow paths
forbidden_uses: random dot grids with no actual topology
using light-dot flows for static, non-relational content
uniform flow speed across all paths hiding meaningful differences

purposes: identify or locate a specific entity within a larger system
give a system element precise technical identity
scene_grammar.composition: A coordinate readout or task-code label appears in mono-scale at the frame edge. Crosshair or registration marks bracket a specific node or panel. The target element brightens to full cyan while surroundings dim.
required_semantics: a real identifiable entity within a system
forbidden_uses: random coordinate strings as sci-fi decoration
fake task codes with no system mapping

entries.semantic_trigger: The shot establishes or maintains the deep-sea spatial environment.
entries.action: Three to four layers of particles float upward at different speeds, creating parallax depth. Closest layer moves fastest with largest particles; deepest layer barely drifts.
entries.result_state: Continuous ambient depth is maintained without competing with active data elements.
entries.hold_policy: Particle motion is continuous and ambient throughout the shot; it must be seek-safe and not rely on infinite loops.

entries.semantic_trigger: A system state is alive, waiting, or processing.
entries.action: The cyan accent on a glass panel or primary metric pulses subtly with a slow呼吸 rhythm, expanding and contracting in brightness.
entries.result_state: The element maintains an alive but non-distracting presence.
entries.hold_policy: Breathing cycle must be slow enough not to draw attention during the reading phase.

entries.semantic_trigger: Data, requests, or resources are moving through the system along a defined path.
entries.action: A cluster of light dots travels along a connecting line from a source node to a destination node, with trailing glow.
entries.result_state: The destination node brightens briefly as the dots arrive, confirming the transfer.
entries.hold_policy: Dots complete their traversal before the reading phase; the result state at the destination holds.

entries.semantic_trigger: A major system state change, chapter boundary, or critical alert.
entries.action: A brief full-frame cyan flash (2-4 frames) bridges a hard cut to the next composition.
entries.result_state: The new composition is fully established; the flash is gone.
entries.hold_policy: No hold on the transition itself.

transitions.semantic_trigger: Standard shot boundary for approximately 80% of transitions.
transitions.action: Immediate cut to the next composition.
transitions.result_state: The next shot is instantly established.

transitions.semantic_trigger: Related shots within the same system or data story segment.
transitions.action: A brief crossfade (6-12 frames) between two compositions, with particles bridging the transition.
transitions.result_state: The new shot is established with a sense of spatial continuity.
transitions.hold_policy: No hold on the transition itself.

global_rules: All motion derives from deterministic local time and must be seek-safe.
Approximately 80% of transitions are hard cuts; crossfades and cyan flash cuts are reserved for chapter boundaries.
Particle layers must never exceed four simultaneous parallax depths to maintain performance.
Cyan breath amplitude is capped at 15% brightness variation to avoid distraction.

modes.usage: Primary presentation with the complete deep-sea environment, particles, HUD panels, and data flows as an opaque frame.
constraints: The deep indigo radial field must be an opaque full-frame background.
Do not add burned-in subtitles or BGM.
verification_requirements: Rendered frame inspection at shot midpoints
Particle layer count and performance verification

modes.usage: Individual glass HUD panels and crisp mono-scale annotations may be isolated as overlays. Particle layers and soft glow must not enter the alpha channel.
constraints: Isolate only opaque glass panel bodies, text, and hard-edge HUD elements.
Move all particles, glow, and semi-transparent glass blur to a separate black-background light layer.
Verify alpha edges carry no soft falloff or color bleed.
verification_requirements: Alpha edge inspection on glass panel boundaries
No particle or glow leakage into alpha

modes.usage: Isolated deep-sea particle layers and cyan glow passes for blend-mode compositing in the target NLE. Light-dot flow networks can also be rendered as standalone light layers.
constraints: Particles and glow must be rendered on true black (#000000) background.
Blend mode must be verified as screen, add, or linear-dodge in the target NLE.
Particle visibility must be tested against varying background luminance.
verification_requirements: Particle visibility test against light and dark backgrounds

hard_rules: Cyan is the only accent color; no secondary signal colors are introduced.
Particle layers are ambient depth and must never compete with the primary data element for attention.
Light-dot flows only appear when there is a real directional or relational data structure.
At most one element at full cyan brightness per shot; everything else uses mid or dim cyan.
do: Use real data, system topologies, and meaningful metrics as the foundation for HUD compositions.
Vary HUD density across shots: some dense multi-panel, some sparse single-focus.
Maintain strict cyan-only accent discipline to preserve the cold data-center identity.
dont: Introduce warm tones, gold, red, or green accents into the deep-sea color space.
Use light-dot flows for static, non-relational content.
Stack more than two glass HUD panels in a single shot.
Use the 10 historically documented exhausted motifs listed in the original CASE-003 project.
Let particles drift uniformly at a single speed and size across all depth layers.

adaptation_knobs.adaptation_goal: Control the number of parallax particle depth layers based on shot complexity and performance budget.
constraints: Reduce to 1-2 layers for hard-alpha or black-background-light modes.
Never exceed 4 layers even on high-performance machines.

adaptation_knobs.adaptation_goal: Control how many distinct HUD elements (panels, flows, coordinate readouts) appear simultaneously.
constraints: Reduce to 1 for emotional or concluding shots.
Never exceed 3 simultaneous HUD element groups.

adaptation_knobs.adaptation_goal: Adjust cyan edge glow and breath amplitude to match content energy level.
constraints: Never exceed 0.8 to avoid bloom washing out glass panel text.
Reduce for quiet analytical segments, increase for high-stakes reveals.

adaptation_knobs.adaptation_goal: Shift the hard-cut to crossfade ratio from the default 80/20 based on content pacing.
constraints: Aggressive: 90% hard cuts with more cyan flash cuts.
Calm: 70% hard cuts with longer crossfades.

inspiration_atoms.adaptation: Apply the strict single-accent discipline from ClickHouse electric-yellow and Supabase emerald-green to the cyan-only system. The cyan accent has three brightness tiers but no competing hue. State indicators use saturation shifts within the cyan family, not additional colors.

Borrow the hard-edge, low-radius, shadow-free panel treatment from NVIDIA and HashiCorp for the non-glass HUD variant. Apply only to the mono-scale and coordinate layer, while glass panels retain their depth material.

Constrain glow, particles, and atmospheric effects to the deep-sea environment following the Stripe and Framer principle of localizing atmosphere rather than blanketing the full frame. Particles live in the abyss, not over glass panels.

signature_motifs.description: Multi-layer floating particles at distinct parallax depths creating an infinite cold deep-sea spatial environment, combined with a single electric cyan accent and glass HUD panels.
Light dots traveling along connecting lines between system nodes to encode data direction, volume, and priority.

exhausted_motifs.reason: Four identical cards in a 2x2 stagger contradicts the asymmetric spatial depth system. Use non-symmetric layouts, pipeline flows, or single-panel focus instead.
A spinning SVG gear is a hollow proxy for system or process. Use actual data flows or topology maps.
Conic gradient gauge rings with needles are only valid for real gauge semantics and must not be the default metric display.
A door rotating open to indicate passage or access. Use safety-gate from soft-aurora-workbench or choose one gate/barrier metaphor per project.
Bar chart overshoot and bounce-back is prohibited in data visualization as it implies incorrect values.
Stroke-dashoffset progress rings are not the default progress expression. Use bar charts, bare numbers, or path-length encodings for real proportions.
Dot waterfall turning green after filtering is no longer the default selection or conversion template.
A glowing AI orb with data flying into it replaces real processes with a generic symbol. Use actual topology, pipeline, or module relationships.
Background gradient drift combined with a bottom progress bar scaleX is prohibited as meaningless universal rhythm filler.
Terminal code scrolling is not a default visual for system or data content. Only show real, readable code when it is the actual evidence.

conflicts_with.reason: A cold deep-sea particle data center and a warm physical-object editing studio occupy opposite worldviews: abstract infinite scale vs. tangible human scale.
conflicts_with.resolution: Borrow at most one data-structure scene pattern from greenroom-writing, restyled with glass and cyan materials. Never borrow paper, warm lamp, or physical object materials.

conflicts_with.reason: Both use blue-black glass and light effects. The deep-sea particle world and the soft aurora workbench world are the highest collision-risk pair in the library.
conflicts_with.resolution: Deep-current uses particles and data flows; aurora-workbench uses aurora video and workbench assembly. Never mix deep-sea particle parallax with aurora glow in the same shot. Keep the two signature motif sets entirely separate.

borrowable_patterns.description: A portable node-and-flow topology layout without the deep-sea particle or cyan material signature.
conditions: The content contains a real directional or network structure.
The borrowing template restyles nodes, lines, and flow indicators with its own material system.

restrictions: Do not distribute source media, private copy, or local paths.
Trademark, font, photo, product UI, and brand copy rights are not included.

forbidden_materials: private source media and business copy
brand logos, proprietary fonts, photos, product interfaces, and claims
original CASE-003 fixed total duration, 4K specs, Google Fonts CDN references, and specific task codes

removed_categories: fixed total duration and 4K pixel specifications
Google Fonts CDN and browser cache assumptions

stale_rules.original_claim: Ambient particle motion must be attached to a timeline and bare animation loops are prohibited.
stale_rules.isolation_reason: The intent of deterministic seek-safe ambient motion is correct, but the specific API constraints must be verified against current HyperFrames core and keyframes skills.

stale_rules.original_claim: Every screen boundary must have a transition; transition IS the exit of the previous shot.
stale_rules.isolation_reason: Conflicts with CASE-004's opposite claim. Most real production cases rely primarily on hard cuts. Transitions are a director choice, not a global requirement.

stale_rules.original_claim: Fixed 2880x2160 pixel dimensions, font sizes, safe areas, and 30fps from the original project.
stale_rules.isolation_reason: Pixel values only apply to the original aspect ratio. Schema stores relative roles and a reference canvas; actual dimensions must be derived per target aspect ratio.
